script: Teammates were annoying so I made them the best brownies of their life. I was grouped with a couple of teammates on a group project. They were the classic vegetarian idealists—always preaching about the planet while I just wanted a solid plan. I couldn't ignore the audacity. They tossed comments like, "I could never be okay with having a ham sandwich," or "You should have cycled today instead of coming with your car." I felt the heat. They wanted to hit up farmers' markets to talk sustainable agriculture. I thought it was a pointless field trip that would eat into deadlines. I said no, that I'd pull my weight from the lab, not the field. They left the next week, and I stayed. They spent three days of our final week on this. But here's the thing, I was left alone to crunch numbers while they did a footnote. The stakes were high; if this didn't work, I'd lose the grade. We decided on a potluck to wind down. I had a killer brownie recipe—so moist, so flavor‑rich, so flawless I'd never tasted a better one. I was about to unleash the bomb. They devoured the tray, begged for seconds, then begged for the recipe. I promised to send it later but kept making excuses. The hype was real. We finished the project, got good grades, and went our separate ways. But wait — it gets worse. Years later, a group member DM'd me for the recipe. I ignored them. I felt satisfied. I just…
